touch_layout.evidence: The deck screens' touch layout (decoded 0xD5D38): records of five 32-bit words, x, y, width, height and the handler's run-time address, read by the touch dispatcher; SH-4 code is 2-byte aligned. In emulation (2026-10-15): touching each zone ran the handler its record names (breakpoints), and a record poked after boot moved the zone.

beat_loop.button_count.evidence: The PERFORM screen's six BEAT LOOP buttons (docs/xdj700-flashing.md, stage 5).

beat_loop.lengths.evidence: The stock buttons set 1/2 to 16 beats; the player's length list also holds 32, which a button set on an owner's unit (docs/xdj700-flashing.md, stage 5, 2026-10-09).

usb.description: The USB source button; with a stick in, it opens the stick's browser (emulator, 2026-10-09).

rotary_push.description: Pushing the rotary selector: in the browser it opens the highlighted entry or loads the track (emulator, 2026-10-09).

state_memory.evidence: The current loop's length in beats, as a fraction: the numerator, then the denominator (32 bits each). In emulation (2026-10-11; four boots of stock, stage 5 and stage 7 with the same stick): 0 and 0 before any loop; each BEAT LOOP pad touched sets it to the length the pad selects (stock 1/2 to 16, stage 5's sixth pad 32, stage 7 1 to 32), and it holds after. Above the loaded application (0x08000000 to 0x091BD788).

The six BEAT LOOP pads' lit states, left to right (32 bits each): 2 lit, 0 not. In emulation (2026-10-11; the same runs): stock lights the touched pad; stage 5 lights none for its 32-beat loop, and stage 7 as first published (0.12) the pad to the right of the touched one and none for 32; stage 7 with its lit list (0.14, 2026-10-16) lights the touched pad, 32 included, as docs/xdj700-flashing.md, "The lit BEAT LOOP pad", describes. Above the loaded application (0x08000000 to 0x091BD788).

The index of the BEAT LOOP pad touched last, 0 to 5 from the left (32 bits): 0 before any touch. In emulation (2026-10-11; the same runs): each pad touched sets its index, on stock, stage 5 and stage 7 alike. Above the loaded application (0x08000000 to 0x091BD788).

restore.official: The unit accepts it over a build, which reports a lower version than 1.15, and it writes back the stock application (stages 4 and 6, on an owner's unit).
restore.backup: The stock no-op rebuild labelled Ver1.16, built without --report-version (the stage-1b file): check its SHA-256 before flashing, since the stage files share its name and label; untested over a modified application (section 3, step 5).
